title: Why Use Redis from DuckDB?
description: Read and write a [Redis](https://redis.io/docs/latest/) instance directly from SQL — no app-layer Python or Node.js glue between DuckDB and the cache. Best for operational queries, hot-cold data joins, and one-off migrations; for application-grade Redis access, keep a real client.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Redis is the most common in-memory cache and quick-lookup store. This extension makes it queryable from inside DuckDB so you don't have to build a Python or Node.js bridge for the common SQL-side workflows.

bulletPoints.label: Hot-cold data joins
bulletPoints.description: Keep recent or frequently-accessed records in Redis, the bulk in DuckDB; join across the boundary with a regular SQL `JOIN` and per-row `redis_get` / `redis_hgetall` lookups.

bulletPoints.label: Bulk migration and audits
bulletPoints.description: Dump an entire Redis keyspace into a DuckDB table with `redis_hscan_over_scan` — one query, server-friendly cursor pagination, ready for offline analysis or export.

bulletPoints.label: Cache priming
bulletPoints.description: Push computed values from DuckDB into Redis with `redis_set` / `redis_hset` so downstream applications hit a warm cache.

bulletPoints.label: Operational queries
bulletPoints.description: Count keys by pattern, sample hashes, find the largest values, or audit a keyspace without writing a Redis-aware tool. Use `redis_scan` for production-safe pagination instead of [`KEYS`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/keys/).

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Every `redis_*` function takes a trailing `secret` argument naming a DuckDB secret of `TYPE redis`. The extension opens a connection per call (with internal pooling) and speaks the [Redis Serialization Protocol](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/reference/protocol-spec/) over plain TCP. There is no `ATTACH` interface — this is purely a function-based extension.

bulletPoints.label: Hashes
bulletPoints.description: `redis_hget` ([`HGET`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/hget/)), `redis_hset` ([`HSET`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/hset/)), `redis_hgetall` ([`HGETALL`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/hgetall/)), `redis_hscan` ([`HSCAN`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/hscan/)) — for the schema-light record pattern most apps use.

bulletPoints.label: Lists
bulletPoints.description: `redis_lpush` ([`LPUSH`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/lpush/)), `redis_lrange`, `redis_lrange_table` — push and read; the `_table` variant emits one row per element instead of a comma-joined string.

bulletPoints.label: Discovery
bulletPoints.description: `redis_keys` ([`KEYS`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/keys/)) for development, `redis_scan` ([`SCAN`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/scan/)) for production. `redis_hscan_over_scan` chains both into a streaming `(key, field, value)` row source — the most useful single function in the extension.

sections.title: Production caveats
sections.description: Be aware before pointing this at a busy Redis instance. The extension is honest-by-design about what it doesn't yet do.

bulletPoints.label: Use SCAN, not KEYS
bulletPoints.description: [`KEYS`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/keys/) blocks the Redis server for the duration of the scan — fine in dev, dangerous on production keyspaces. Prefer `redis_scan` and `redis_hscan_over_scan`, which use cursor-paginated [`SCAN`](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/scan/) under the hood.

bulletPoints.label: Strings, hashes, and lists only
bulletPoints.description: No SET / ZSET / STREAM / PUB-SUB / TRANSACTIONS / SCRIPTING today. See [Redis data types](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/) for what's supported elsewhere.

bulletPoints.label: Single-node connections
bulletPoints.description: No [Redis Cluster](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/scaling/) topology awareness. Point the secret at a single endpoint.

bulletPoints.label: Plaintext auth
bulletPoints.description: The `password` field in the secret is sent over plain TCP — TLS is not yet wired up. Use the extension on trusted networks until that lands. See [Redis security](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/security/) for the upstream guidance.

bulletPoints.label: Experimental status
bulletPoints.description: The function surface may change as more Redis primitives land. Pin a known-good extension version in production CTAS jobs.

useCases.title: Drain a Redis keyspace into DuckDB
useCases.description: One [`CREATE TABLE AS`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_table) wrapping `redis_hscan_over_scan` — usually the fastest path from "every `user:*` hash in production" to a queryable Parquet/CSV-ready dataset.

useCases.title: Join cached lookups against bulk data
useCases.description: Per-row `redis_get` / `redis_hgetall` lookups inside a `SELECT` against a wide DuckDB table. Works because DuckDB pipelines the lookups; for very wide joins, consider materializing the Redis side via `redis_hscan_over_scan` first.

useCases.title: Audit a production keyspace
useCases.description: Count keys by prefix, sample hashes, find outliers — using `redis_scan` so the audit doesn't stall the Redis server. Easier than writing a Python script for each one-off question.

useCases.title: Prime a cache from analytical output
useCases.description: Compute aggregates in DuckDB, then push them with `redis_set` / `redis_hset` so the application layer hits a warm cache. Single SQL query end-to-end.
